ai_summary:
Scottish wind generation is currently delivering an estimated 2.6 GW, representing 25.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity, while total GB wind output stands at 5.5 GW across the wider network. This substantial low-carbon contribution suppresses Scottish carbon intensity to a remarkably low 4 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide average of 181 gCO2/kWh. However, persistent cross-border transmission bottlenecks prevent this abundant renewable power from reaching southern demand centres. 

Consequently, 1,044 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £38,773. To compensate for this turned-down power and maintain network balance, an estimated 198,303 m3 of gas had to be burned elsewhere, generating an avoidable 365 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. Annualising this operational pattern indicates an estimated total yearly cost of £14 million for Scottish wind curtailment. When distributed across national electricity consumption, this volume of curtailment translates to an estimated increase of approximately £0.05/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the dual financial and environmental penalties imposed by grid infrastructure limitations.
